agree.reason: Because the memo gives the renovation real credit, the GM's own view goes unchallenged and the claim becomes believable; the case on training, turnover and the seven weeks of cover is solid, but it never says why it beats someone who ran a bigger desk.

honest.reason: It rightly drops the 'main reason' claim that the facts can't support, and the derived figures (almost half the training time, about 70% fewer training shifts) are labelled as resting on an assumption and are close to accurate.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the turnover figures into rates (two in three down to one in three) and links training and turnover to payroll through the 81-versus-25 shift count, but it misses that the score is specifically for check-in, which the desk controls more directly than any room renovation.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison to the outside hire is 'no handover', which is thin; it doesn't weigh larger-hotel experience against six years here and the improvements in this specific building.

qualification.reason: The budget plan includes a three-month monthly review with the GM, which he can check, but it sets no number or tolerance for payroll variance and says nothing about what happens if results fall short.

objections.reason: It meets the renovation objection by conceding it and meets the lack of budget experience with a plan and a cost link, but it doesn't directly answer the outside candidate's larger-hotel experience.

fit.reason: It's a concise, one-page memo addressed to the GM, which is what was asked for.
